analysis.title: Diversify beyond the AI rally (UBS House View - Daily US)
key_insights: US equities rose Monday on a tech-led rally: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained 2.8% and the Nasdaq rose 0.8%. Tech fundraising was the main focus.
Tech financing deals: Broadcom arranged a USD 63bn deal to finance chip purchases, SpaceX signed a roughly USD 40bn equipment-finance lease, and Meta raised its equity fundraising to USD 97.5bn.
UBS expects AI demand to remain a key growth engine and says the coming days of hyperscaler September-quarter results should show more evidence on the sustainability and monetization of that demand.

UBS stays constructive on structural AI growth but says high expectations and wide differences in company outcomes raise single-stock concentration risk. It advises broadly diversified equity portfolios.
UBS suggests long-term growth investors also consider the Power and resources and Longevity themes alongside AI.

Power and resources: demand is driven by AI and electrification needing data centers, power generation, grids and related infrastructure. An improving automation cycle and stronger metals prices add support. UBS favors a selective approach and prefers companies with visible multi-year demand, credible capacity expansion, disciplined balance sheets and the ability to protect margins amid elevated input costs and interest rates.

Longevity: aging populations and clinical innovation sustain demand. Recent earnings point to moderating medical procedure demand, but low penetration and this year's significant valuation reset support the long-term case. UBS is also positive on obesity treatments as greater supply and lower pricing broaden patient access.

UBS stays positive on Eurozone equities (manufacturing recovery, structural investment, improving operating leverage), sees Asian valuations at multi-decade lows with AI investment and cyclical recovery supporting earnings, and expects Japanese equities to benefit from AI capex, cyclical improvement and corporate reform.

EURUSD fell to 1.1155 on Tuesday morning after four straight daily declines. The DXY index rose above 102. UBS reads this as a US dollar rebound rather than Europe-specific stress, and expects EURUSD to recover toward 1.16 by year-end. It likes selling the downside in EURUSD for yield pickup.
The French-German 10-year yield spread narrowed by 13 basis points to about 153 basis points on Monday after Moody's did not deliver a widely expected downgrade of France.

Brazil sold off Monday after Lula won a fourth term with 51.8% of valid votes. The Ibovespa closed 13.9% lower, its largest daily fall since March 2020, with a 30-minute trading halt. The real fell more than 11% intraday and closed 8.1% lower at 5.415 per dollar. Five-year CDS rose to 144 basis points from 120, and the Treasury canceled two bond auctions.

UBS says fiscal credibility is the main test for Brazil. Public debt exceeds 80% of GDP and stabilizing it could require a primary balance improvement of around 3.5% of GDP. UBS expects higher interest rates for longer, firmer inflation pressure, weaker growth and less support for Brazilian risk assets until clarity emerges on the economic team and fiscal plan.
Events to watch on 28 October: Fed rate decision, Microsoft, Alphabet, Ford and GE Vernova earnings, Australia September inflation, and the Bank of Canada rate decision.

sector_views.rationale: Structural demand from AI and electrification investment in data centers, power generation and grids, plus an improving automation cycle and stronger metals prices. UBS favors a selective approach.
Aging demographics, clinical innovation, low penetration and a significant valuation reset this year, despite moderating medical procedure demand in recent earnings. Positive on obesity treatments.
Constructive on structural AI growth, but high expectations and wide outcome differences argue for diversification away from single-stock concentration.

earnings_insights: Hyperscaler September-quarter results are due in the coming days. UBS expects them to show evidence on the sustainability and monetization of AI demand.
Microsoft, Alphabet, Ford and GE Vernova report on 28 October.
Recent health care earnings point to moderating medical procedure demand (no figures given).
